blocks.html: Software verification is the process of testing whether or not the software works as expected in all cases. A unit test is a test designed to test a small portion of the code (typically a function or call) in isolation to ensure a particular behavior occurs as expected. Unit test frameworks can help you organize your unit tests. Integration testing tests the integration of a bunch of units together to ensure they work properly.
blocks.preview: Software verification is the process of testing whether or not the software work
blocks.html_cs: Verifikace softwaru (software verification) je proces testování, zda software funguje podle očekávání ve všech případech. Jednotkový test (unit test) je test navržený k izolovanému otestování malé části kódu (typicky funkce nebo volání), aby se zajistilo, že se chová podle očekávání. Testovací frameworky pro jednotkové testy (unit test frameworks) vám mohou pomoci jednotkové testy organizovat. Integrační testování (integration testing) testuje propojení skupiny jednotek dohromady, aby se ověřilo, že spolu fungují správně.

blocks.html: Code coverage refers to how much of the source code is executed while testing. Statement coverage refers to the percentage of statements in a program that have been exercised by testing routines. Branch coverage refers to the percentage of branches that have been executed by testing routines. Loop coverage (also called the 0, 1, 2 test) means that if you have a loop, you should ensure it works properly when it iterates 0 times, 1 time, and 2 times.
blocks.preview: Code coverage refers to how much of the source code is executed while testing. S
blocks.html_cs: Pokrytí kódu (code coverage) označuje, jak velká část zdrojového kódu se během testování vykoná. Pokrytí příkazů (statement coverage) označuje procento příkazů v programu, které byly vykonány testovacími rutinami. Pokrytí větví (branch coverage) označuje procento větví kódu, které byly vykonány testovacími rutinami. Pokrytí smyček (loop coverage, nazývané také test 0, 1, 2) znamená, že pokud máte smyčku, měli byste se ujistit, že funguje správně, když proběhne 0krát, 1krát a 2krát.

blocks.html: The happy path is the path of execution that occurs when there are no errors encountered. A sad path is one where an error or failure state occurs. A non-recoverable error (also called a fatal error) is an error that is severe enough that the program can’t continue running. A program that handles error cases well is robust.
blocks.preview: The happy path is the path of execution that occurs when there are no errors enc
blocks.html_cs: Happy path (příznivá cesta) je cesta provádění programu, která nastane, když nedojde k žádným chybám. Sad path (nepříznivá cesta) je ta, kde nastane chyba nebo selhání. Neobnovitelná chyba (také nazývaná fatální chyba / fatal error) je chyba natolik závažná, že program nemůže pokračovat v běhu. Program, který dobře zvládá chybové stavy, je robustní.

blocks.html: A precondition is any condition that must always be true prior to the execution of some segment of code. An invariant is a condition that must be true while some component is executing. A postcondition is any condition that must always be true after the execution of some code.
blocks.preview: A precondition is any condition that must always be true prior to the execution
blocks.html_cs: Prekondice je jakákoli podmínka, která musí být vždy splněna před vykonáním určitého úseku kódu. Invariant je podmínka, která musí platit po celou dobu provádění určité komponenty. Postkondice je jakákoli podmínka, která musí být vždy splněna po vykonání určitého kódu.

blocks.html: An assertion is an expression that will be true unless there is a bug in the program. In C++, runtime assertions are typically implemented using the assert preprocessor macro. Assertions are usually turned off in non-debug code. A static_assert is an assertion that is evaluated at compile-time.
blocks.preview: An assertion is an expression that will be true unless there is a bug in the pro
blocks.html_cs: Aserce je výraz, který je pravdivý, pokud v programu není chyba. V C++ jsou runtime aserce obvykle implementovány pomocí preprocesorového makra assert. V ne-debug kódu bývají aserce obvykle vypnuté. static_assert je aserce vyhodnocovaná v době překladu (compile-time).

blocks.html: Assertions should be used to document cases that should be logically impossible. Error handling should be used to handle cases that are possible.

blocks.questionHtml: In a quiz for lesson 8.x -- Chapter 8 summary and quiz, we implemented a game of Hi-Lo.
blocks.solutionHtml:
#include <iostream>
#include <limits>   // for std::numeric_limits
#include "Random.h" // https://www.learncpp.com/cpp-tutorial/global-random-numbers-random-h/

int getGuess(int count, int min, int max)
{
	while (true) // loop until user enters valid input
	{
		std::cout << "Guess #" << count << ": ";

		int guess {};
		std::cin >> guess;

		bool success { std::cin };
		std::cin.clear(); // put us back in 'normal' operation mode (if needed)
		std::cin.ignore(std::numeric_limits<std::streamsize>::max(), '\n'); // remove any extra input

		// If we didn't extract anything or the extracted guess is out of bounds, try again
		if (!success || guess < min || guess > max)
			continue;

		return guess;
	}
}

// returns true if the user won, false if they lost
bool playHiLo(int guesses, int min, int max)
{
	std::cout << "Let's play a game. I'm thinking of a number between " << min << " and " << max << ". You have " << guesses << " tries to guess what it is.\n";
	int number{ Random::get(min, max) }; // this is the number the user needs to guess

	// Loop through all of the guesses
	for (int count{ 1 }; count <= guesses; ++count)
	{
		int guess{ getGuess(count, min, max) };

		if (guess > number)
			std::cout << "Your guess is too high.\n";
		else if (guess < number)
			std::cout << "Your guess is too low.\n";
		else // guess == number, so the user won
		{
			std::cout << "Correct! You win!\n";
			return true;
		}
	}

	// The user lost
	std::cout << "Sorry, you lose. The correct number was " << number << '\n';
	return false; // if the user lost
}

bool playAgain()
{
	// Keep asking the user if they want to play again until they pick y or n.
	while (true)
	{
		char ch{};
		std::cout << "Would you like to play again (y/n)? ";
		std::cin >> ch;

		// clear out any extraneous input
		std::cin.ignore(std::numeric_limits<std::streamsize>::max(), '\n');
        
		switch (ch)
		{
		case 'y': return true;
		case 'n': return false;
		}
	}
}

int main()
{
	constexpr int guesses { 7 }; // the user has this many guesses
	constexpr int min     { 1 };
	constexpr int max     { 100 };

	do
	{
		playHiLo(guesses, min, max);
	} while (playAgain());

	std::cout << "Thank you for playing.\n";

	return 0;
}
